front.title: Elliptic Curves for Security: X25519's Diffie-Hellman vector

abstract.t: A fixture, not a specification: the Diffie-Hellman test vector of RFC 7748 Section 6.1, cited under the labels the RFC prints it with, from spec to a run of the reference X25519 in tests/fixtures/x25519. Every binding sentence of RFC 7748 is quoted here, and those this fixture does not test are excluded.
This copy is a near miss: it labels Alice's public key X25519(a, 5), an alias Section 6.1 does not print, so fidelity refuses it.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

The module is the reference X25519 of tests/fixtures/x25519/fixture, run with --package fixture=tests/fixtures/x25519/fixture. Each row cites the values of Section 6.1 under the labels the RFC prints them with, such as Alice's private key, a and Alice's public key, X25519(a, 9), so fidelity checks every byte against the RFC.

section.name: Interface
The X25519 Function

blockquote.t: The functions take a scalar and a u-coordinate as inputs and produce a u-coordinate as output.
When receiving such an array, implementations of X25519 (but not X448) MUST mask the most significant bit in the final byte.

section.t: Untested: this fixture checks the Section 6.1 vector only; amritk/nish's specs/rfc7748-x25519.md tests the mask

blockquote.t: Implementations MUST accept non-canonical values and process them as if they had been reduced modulo the field prime.

section.t: Untested: this fixture checks the Section 6.1 vector only; amritk/nish's specs/rfc7748-x25519.md tests non-canonical values

blockquote.t: For X25519, the unused, most significant bit MUST be zero.

section.t: Untested: this fixture checks the Section 6.1 vector only; amritk/nish's specs/rfc7748-x25519.md tests the output's top bit

blockquote.t: The cswap function SHOULD be implemented in constant time (i.e., independent of the swap argument).

section.t: Untested: timing is not observable by a functional test

blockquote.t: Both now share K = X25519(a, X25519(b, 9)) = X25519(b, X25519(a, 9)) as a shared secret.

section.name: Deterministic Generation

blockquote.t: The trace of Frobenius MUST NOT be in {0, 1} in order to rule out the attacks described in [smart], [satoh], and [semaev], as in [brainpool] and [safecurves].

section.t: Untested: an obligation on choosing a curve, which Curve25519 already meets; nothing an implementation of X25519 does can satisfy or violate it

blockquote.t: MOV Degree [reducing]: the embedding degree MUST be greater than (order - 1) / 100, as in [brainpool] and [safecurves].

section.t: Untested: an obligation on choosing a curve, which Curve25519 already meets; nothing an implementation of X25519 does can satisfy or violate it

blockquote.t: CM Discriminant: discriminant D MUST be greater than 2^100, as in [safecurves].

section.t: Untested: an obligation on choosing a curve, which Curve25519 already meets; nothing an implementation of X25519 does can satisfy or violate it

abstract.t: This memo specifies two elliptic curves over prime fields that offer a high level of practical security in cryptographic applications, including Transport Layer Security (TLS). These curves are intended to operate at the ~128-bit and ~224-bit security level, respectively, and are generated deterministically based on a list of required properties.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
